title: serverless_function plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `serverless_function` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component ServerlessFunctionConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

ServerlessFunctionConfig.description:
Plugin: serverless_function — Invokes AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, or
Google Cloud Functions as middleware in the proxy pipeline. The function
is invoked in the finalized-request-egress phase, after request-body
transforms and after every final request-policy hook (WAF body rules,
OpenAPI request schema, body validation, the post-transform request-size
ceiling) has accepted the exact backend-visible body, so those policies
never reject only after the function was contacted. Backend admission,
circuit-breaker, or transport checks can still fail later. In
`pre_proxy` mode the function response can inject request headers and
metadata before the backend call. In `terminate` mode the function
response is returned directly to the client. Native gRPC terminate
requires a JSON contract with `grpc_status` plus optional
`message_base64` (raw protobuf bytes), `grpc_message`,
`status_details_base64`, and custom `trailers`; the gateway frames an
uncompressed unary DATA message and owns reserved terminal metadata.
The request is classified as native gRPC by the HTTP flavor the
frontend stamps at intake, not by a mutable effective content-type.
Every terminal trailer value is bounded by an 8 KiB wire-value
ceiling, measured after sanitization and after base64 or
percent-encoding, and the complete terminal metadata block —
`grpc-status`, `grpc-message`, `grpc-status-details-bin`, every
custom trailer, and `content-type` — is bounded by a separate 16 KiB
aggregate budget charged as name + value + 32 bytes per field, the
way HTTP/2 charges `SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE` and HTTP/3 charges
`SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE`. Custom trailers are additionally
capped at 32 entries. `grpc_message` is authored as human-readable text
and emitted in the canonical percent-encoded `grpc-message` wire form
(uppercase hex for `%` and every byte outside the grammar's
unescaped range). Custom trailers use the gRPC Custom-Metadata name
alphabet and printable-ASCII value grammar; `-bin` values must be
standard base64 with or without padding. Names are case-insensitive,
so two `trailers` members differing only in case are rejected rather
than one silently overwriting the other. The raw function output is
also screened for duplicate JSON object member names before parsing —
byte-identical, escaped-equivalent, or nested inside `trailers` — so a
document whose terminal outcome depends on which parser reads it is
refused instead of resolved.
gRPC-Web terminate is rejected with 500. Streaming and compression
contract shapes fail closed. Malformed or oversized function output
fails closed without reflecting untrusted bodies. The validated
framed response enters the shared response-body policy lifecycle, so
configured gRPC response validators and limits still apply; if a body
policy or transform invalidates that authorized representation, the
response fails closed to a nonzero gRPC error rather than degrading to
an empty successful trailers-only reply. An over-limit raw function
response on a native gRPC terminate request is likewise a mandatory
rejection rather than a fall-through, even with `on_error: continue`.
The same representation is produced on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3:
the HTTP/3 finalized-request-egress rejection is written through the
context-aware writer, so the authored frame, the terminal metadata, and
an original gRPC-Web client's browser framing all survive that
boundary. The status-only shape carries
the same provenance: unchanged, it stays trailers-only and restores its
complete terminal metadata (grpc-status, optional grpc-message,
grpc-status-details-bin, and validated custom trailers) from the
validated contract rather than the reject header map, with an omitted
grpc-message emitted as omission rather than a synthesized reason; a
changed status or an unauthored body fails closed the same way and
discards every authored terminal key with it, and it can never
authorize DATA. Cloud credential
fields fall
back to well-known environment variables. Every recognized provider
field is validated whenever it is SUPPLIED, independently of which
provider the row selects: JSON type, the Lambda Invoke identifier
grammars, the HTTP field-value grammar for credential headers, and the
lexical URL contract. A well-typed, well-formed field belonging to an
inactive provider stays accepted, so changing `provider` later cannot
turn an already-admitted row into a constructor error. Terminate mode forwards
applicable end-to-end response headers, preserving repeated Set-Cookie
and list-valued Link while requiring Location, Content-Location, and
Refresh to remain singleton,
while stripping hop-by-hop, Connection-listed, transport-managed,
provider-control, and credential-bearing fields. URL-valued Location,
Content-Location, Refresh (url= and bare URI forms after semicolon,
comma, or ASCII-whitespace delay separators), and every Link target are removed
when a relative, absolute, encoded, or nested target exposes the
configured signed function path/query. Duplicate singleton URL-valued
fields fail closed instead of being comma-folded; repeated Link lines
are revalidated as the exact combined list returned downstream.
Complete signed paths match at
slash-delimited segment boundaries even with added prefix or descendant
segments, not inside arbitrary substrings. The complete slash-trimmed
signed path is also protected when copied exactly into either side of a
decoded query pair; longer scalar lookalikes remain observable. Both
non-empty components of every configured query pair are protected
credential scalars: a key
remains protected whether it is key-only (`?SIGNED_TOKEN=`) or paired
with a value (`?SIGNED_TOKEN=1`), and a non-empty value is protected
independently. Exact ASCII-case-insensitive URI scheme copies are also
governed. Leading and trailing slashes remain part of each scalar;
a slash-only scalar remains protected and makes ambiguous URL-path
surfaces fail closed. Each scalar remains protected if copied into
either side of another query pair or into decoded paths at URI-component
boundaries (including path-parameter/query delimiters), and decoded fragments are checked
directly at URI-component boundaries even when they are scalar rather
than URI-shaped. Query comparison
percent-decodes generic URI components but preserves literal `+` characters
instead of applying form-data space conversion. Inspection checks
explicit numeric authority ports before normalization can erase default
ports, and is bounded to 16 KiB per field, 32 Link targets, 32 embedded
path URI references, eight percent-decoding transforms, and two nested
URI-reference hops. URI userinfo, residual
encoding, malformed target syntax, malformed percent triplets,
percent-decoded non-UTF-8 bytes, budget overflow, or another structural
URI reference at the nesting boundary fails closed even for root
function destinations, while unrelated URL targets, non-URL
Refresh directives, quoted Link parameters, and scalar labels without
signed components remain observable.
Later body rewrites invalidate ranges, validators, integrity metadata,
and content-bound signatures while unmodified responses retain them;
206 Partial Content and 226 IM Used responses skip rewriting to preserve
range and delta semantics; transform-dependent header hooks also decline
them rather than relabelling untouched bytes. Inspection still runs,
and enforcing
redaction-dependent plugins reject governed content when those bytes
cannot be safely rewritten.
Proven pre-invocation payload-validation, unsupported-gRPC-Web,
DNS-policy,
and literal-IP-policy rejections release every acquired deduplication
owner after commit. Real remote 502 responses remain application
responses; uncertain post-invocation failures retain their protection.
Deduplicated terminal replays preserve the final status/body but use
sanitized headers: session/authentication fields, Retry-After,
trace/correlation fields, and rate-limit counters are not replayed. The
stored body is already finalized and bypasses ordinary presentation
transforms on replay while remaining subject to response inspection and
final-body validation. A current-policy redaction decision runs only its
required transform and fails closed with 502 if rewriting cannot
complete.
If request_deduplication is attached, every same-protocol instance must
have a strictly lower effective priority than terminate mode; candidate
admission rejects equal or reversed ordering before persistence. This
candidate check derives static serverless capabilities without resolving
CP-local cloud credentials; runtime construction still validates the
node-local credentials and environment fail closed. CP and admin
admission of the plugin config itself is shape-only for the same
reason: every supplied field is validated, while AWS/Azure/GCP
credentials that intentionally exist only on data planes are resolved
and enforced when the serving node builds its plugin cache. `validate`
therefore checks the shape of the row rather than whether the
validating node holds the credentials the row needs at serve time.
HEAD/204/205/304 bodies are empty. Automatic redirects are disabled;
pre_proxy accepts only 2xx as approval, while terminate may
intentionally return only final 2xx-5xx statuses (200-599).
Informational and out-of-range three-digit function statuses follow the
configured error path. For aws_lambda, every non-2xx Lambda Invoke API
status (throttling, access denied, a missing function, an oversized
payload, a service fault) is authored by the Lambda service rather than
by the function, so it is an invocation failure
(`lambda_service_error`) under `on_error` / `error_status_code` in
every mode, and the AWS error body is never returned.

provider.description: Cloud provider for the serverless function.

mode.description:
pre_proxy: invoke and inject headers/metadata, then continue.
terminate: invoke and return response to client (HTTP body
passthrough, or native-gRPC JSON unary contract).

function_url.description: HTTP(S) trigger URL without URL userinfo or a fragment. Required for azure_functions and gcp_cloud_functions; ignored for aws_lambda invocation (the URL is derived from region + function name), but still validated when supplied, whichever provider is selected. The lexical contract matches runtime admission: a non-empty host (a registered name, an IPv4 literal, or a bracketed IPv6 literal), an optional port of 0-65535, no URL userinfo, no fragment, and no raw ASCII whitespace or control character anywhere in the value. Path/query credentials are structurally redacted from diagnostics and non-admin/audit projections.

aws_region.description: AWS region (aws_lambda only). Falls back to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, then AWS_REGION env vars. The default endpoint is partition-aware: cn-* regions derive lambda.<region>.amazonaws.com.cn and every other region derives lambda.<region>.amazonaws.com. The air-gapped ISO partitions and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud are not derived and require an explicit aws_endpoint_url. When the key id or secret resolves from the process environment, the region must be a lowercase commercial, GovCloud, or China region (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials).

aws_access_key_id.description: IAM access key (aws_lambda only). Falls back to AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID env var. The key id is interpolated into the SigV4 Authorization header, so the effective config or environment value must be representable as an HTTP field value (no NUL, CR, LF, or other control byte except horizontal tab); validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected. A process-environment credential may only be signed for an official AWS Lambda endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). Not allowed with aws_credentials: default_chain.

aws_secret_access_key.description: IAM secret key (aws_lambda only). Falls back to AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY env var. A process-environment credential may only be signed for an official AWS Lambda endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). Not allowed with aws_credentials: default_chain.

aws_function_name.description: Lambda function name, partial ARN, or full ARN (aws_lambda only), matching the Lambda Invoke API FunctionName grammar. Falls back to AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME env var; the environment value is held to the same grammar. Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected. Existence and invoke permission are not checked at admission.

aws_session_token.description: STS session token (aws_lambda only). Falls back to AWS_SESSION_TOKEN env var only when aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key also resolve from the environment; the environment token is never paired with a config key pair. Sent verbatim as x-amz-security-token, so the effective value must be representable as an HTTP field value (no NUL, CR, LF, or other control byte except horizontal tab). A process-environment token may only be sent to an official AWS Lambda endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). Not allowed with aws_credentials: default_chain.

aws_qualifier.description: Optional version/alias qualifier (e.g., $LATEST, prod), matching the Lambda Invoke API Qualifier grammar. Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected.

aws_endpoint_url.description: Optional HTTP(S) Lambda endpoint override for LocalStack or a VPC-internal endpoint. Must be an origin without userinfo, path, query, or fragment, using the same lexical URL contract as `function_url` (non-empty host, port 0-65535, no raw whitespace or control characters). Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected. Falls back to `AWS_LAMBDA_ENDPOINT_URL`. A non-default port is part of the signed SigV4 canonical `Host`, so a verifying endpoint accepts the invocation. When the AWS key id or secret resolves from the process environment, a configured override must be an official AWS Lambda endpoint unless `allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials` is true (see that field); an `AWS_LAMBDA_ENDPOINT_URL` fallback is set by the same environment owner and is trusted like the environment credentials.

aws_credentials.description: aws_lambda only. `static` (default) signs with a literal key pair from the config or from the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) environment variables, resolved once when the plugin is built. `default_chain` signs with the gateway process's own AWS identity from the AWS SDK default credential chain — environment variables, shared config/credentials profiles, web identity (EKS IRSA), ECS container credentials, and EC2 instance metadata (IMDSv2) — cached and refreshed in the background before expiry, so temporary workload credentials keep working without a reload. A request waits (bounded) only when no usable credential is cached; expired credentials are never used, and an unavailable chain is an invocation failure (`aws_credentials_unavailable`) under `on_error`. `default_chain` may not be combined with aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key, or aws_session_token, and is subject to the same ambient endpoint scope as process-environment credentials (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). It requires a build with the `secrets-aws` (or `cloud-secrets`) Cargo feature: CP/admin shape-only admission accepts the row, and a serving node built without the feature refuses to construct it.

allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_crede.description: aws_lambda only. When `aws_access_key_id` or `aws_secret_access_key` is omitted from the config and resolves from the gateway process environment (`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` is then used too; it never completes a config key pair), or when `aws_credentials` is `default_chain`, `aws_region` must be a lowercase commercial, GovCloud, or China region, and the config-chosen Lambda endpoint (the host derived from `aws_region`, or the `aws_endpoint_url` override) must be an official AWS Lambda endpoint for that region over HTTPS on the default port: lambda[-fips].<region>.amazonaws.com, lambda[-fips].<region>.api.aws, or an interface VPC endpoint vpce-<id>[-<az>].lambda[-fips].<region>.vpce.amazonaws.com, where <region> is a commercial or GovCloud region; a cn-* region uses amazonaws.com.cn and the dual-stack api.amazonwebservices.com.cn instead. An `AWS_LAMBDA_ENDPOINT_URL` set in the environment (used only when the config sets no `aws_endpoint_url`) is trusted like the environment credentials. Anything else is refused at configuration admission (CP/admin shape-only admission screens a configured `aws_region` and `aws_endpoint_url` whenever the config omits the key pair), and every invocation re-checks the endpoint and fails closed with 500 (`ambient_credential_endpoint_refused`) regardless of `on_error`. Credentials written into the config are not scoped. Set true only to deliberately sign invocations for a private endpoint (for example LocalStack), an air-gapped ISO partition, or the AWS European Sovereign Cloud with the process credentials; anyone who can write this plugin config can then direct those credentials to that endpoint.

azure_function_key.description: Function key for x-functions-key auth (azure_functions only). Falls back to the FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_AZURE_FUNCTIONS_KEY env var (never the ambient AZURE_FUNCTIONS_KEY, because the key is sent to the config-chosen function_url). The value must be representable as an HTTP field value (no NUL, CR, LF, or other control byte except horizontal tab); the effective config or environment value is parsed at admission so an unusable credential never reaches the serving cache. Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected.

gcp_bearer_token.description: Bearer token for Authorization header (gcp_cloud_functions only). Falls back to the FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_GCP_CLOUD_FUNCTIONS_BEARER_TOKEN env var (never the ambient GCP_CLOUD_FUNCTIONS_BEARER_TOKEN). The assembled `Bearer <token>` value must be representable as an HTTP field value (no NUL, CR, LF, or other control byte except horizontal tab) and is parsed at admission. Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected.

payload_format.description: `ferrum` (default) sends the Ferrum invocation payload and uses the Ferrum response contracts. `aws_api_gateway_v2` (aws_lambda with mode terminate only) sends an API Gateway HTTP API proxy event, payload format 2.0 (`version`, `routeKey`, `rawPath`, `rawQueryString`, `cookies`, `headers`, `queryStringParameters`, `requestContext`, `body`, `isBase64Encoded`), built from the same finalized request view and the same fail-closed forward_headers / forward_query_params / forward_body selection, and maps the function result like an API Gateway proxy integration: a JSON object with `statusCode` (integer 200-599) is a structured response with optional `headers`, `multiValueHeaders`, `cookies` (one Set-Cookie each), `body`, and `isBase64Encoded`, with an identical name/value pair in `headers` and `multiValueHeaders` merged into one field line and at most 128 header field lines / 32 KiB of header names and values; a JSON string result is returned as the decoded string and any other JSON value as its JSON text, both with status 200 and content-type application/json. Mapped headers are sanitized like provider response headers. A duplicate-member or malformed result fails with `invalid_api_gateway_response` under `on_error`. Native gRPC terminate requests are refused before invocation with `unsupported_grpc_payload_format`.

forward_body.description: Include one authoritative lossless finalized request-body representation in the function payload for every HTTP method. Ferrum never parses JSON into a structured value: exact UTF-8 bytes are carried as a string with body_encoding=utf8, arbitrary bytes are base64 with body_encoding=base64, and the active hook Content-Type is carried separately as body_content_type. The plugin buffers before invocation and fails closed if bytes are unavailable or either the original or active request headers use a non-identity Content-Encoding. Because invocation occurs after request-body transforms and final request-policy acceptance, this plugin may share a protocol chain with a request-body transformer and observes the exact backend-visible bytes. Candidate admission and runtime cache construction retain the fail-closed composition refusal only for registered custom plugins that declare pre-finalization request-body egress.

forward_headers.description: Each entry must be a non-empty RFC 9110 HTTP field-name token (no empty string, spaces, or other separators), matching runtime admission. Header names to forward into the function payload (lowercased at config load). Values come from the finalized backend-visible header view (the function is invoked in the finalized-request-egress phase, after request-body transforms and every final request-policy hook), so a header an earlier plugin removed - authorization under strip_authorization_on_success, or a gateway-owned claim_headers destination with no verified claim - is omitted rather than re-read from the client's original request.

forward_query_params.description: Include decoded query parameters from the shared canonical backend-bound query view in the function payload, after omitting credentials that an earlier auth plugin marked for backend stripping. Behavior is identical on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 and includes any earlier ordered query transform. Duplicate decoded names (including percent-encoded aliases and bare/valued pairs), literal '+', an unencoded ';' ('%3B' is unambiguous), malformed percent-encoding, non-UTF-8 decodings, and parameters lacking their original encoded representation are rejected before invocation even when on_error=continue.

timeout_ms.description: Function invocation timeout in milliseconds, 1-900000 (15 minutes, the AWS Lambda synchronous invocation maximum). A larger value is rejected at admission.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Max function response body size (10 MiB default), 1-67108864 (64 MiB). The response is buffered whole, so this is the per-invocation retained-memory ceiling; a larger value is rejected at admission.

on_error.description: reject: return error to client. continue: skip and proxy normally.

error_status_code.description: Final HTTP error status when rejecting an invocation or pre_proxy non-2xx response. Must be in range 400-599.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit an http:// function_url or aws_endpoint_url whose host is not a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1]. The invocation payload and the provider credential (function key, bearer token, or SigV4 signature) then cross the network in clear. The AWS_LAMBDA_ENDPOINT_URL environment fallback is operator-controlled and is not screened. Omit for false; an explicit null is rejected like every other optional field.
